title: ZDX collections: default collections, membership, ranking, criteria, deletion and limits

prose.text: A collection is how the console groups applications with their probes. {{what}} {{default-collections}}

prose.label: Membership.
prose.text: {{membership}} The managed side's default collection is named two ways {{divergence:managed-default-collection-name}}.

prose.label: Ranking.
prose.text: {{ranking}} How drag-and-drop ranking combines with the alphabetical rule, and what ranking changes for an application in several collections, is not stated {{gap:collection-ranking}}.

prose.label: Criteria.
prose.text: {{collection-criteria}} What an application in a collection does with its own probing criteria is in [[zdx.probes.criteria:collection-overrides]]. {{collection-fields}} Whether managed collections have criteria is open {{gap:managed-collection-criteria}}.

prose.label: Removing, deleting and disabling.
prose.text: {{remove-app}} {{delete-app}} {{delete-collection}} Deleting a managed collection is described two ways {{divergence:managed-collection-delete}}, and so is deleting a probe on its own {{divergence:probe-deletion}}. {{enable-disable}}

prose.label: In the API.
prose.text: The contract's collection operations are not read here {{gap:collections-api}}.

what.statement: A collection organizes applications with their probes: configuring an application assigns it to a collection and then configures its probes, and a collection can instead be created first and the application and probe added later.

quotes: A collection is useful in organizing and categorizing your applications with their probes.

When you configure an application, you assign it to a collection and then configure the corresponding probes to it. Optionally, you can create a collection as needed and then add the application and probe at a later time.

default-collections.statement: The End User collection starts with three collections, the Unified Communication Collection, the Predefined Apps Collection and the Custom Apps Collection, and these default collections cannot be deleted.

quotes: The End User collection starts with three types of collections called Unified Communication Collection, Predefined Apps Collection, and Custom Apps Collection.
You cannot delete a default collection (e.g., Unified Communication Collection, Predefined Apps Collection, Custom Apps Collection).
You cannot delete the default collections (i.e., Unified Communication Collection, Predefined Apps Collection, Custom Apps Collection).

membership.statement: A configured application in an End User collection can be in several collections, while a configured application for Managed Monitoring can exist in only one collection, so removing it from that collection also removes all its associated probes.

quotes: A configured application in an End User collection can be in multiple collections.
A configured application for Managed Monitoring can exist in only one collection.
For Managed collections, you can configure an application for only one collection. Therefore, if you remove the application from a collection, it also removes all the associated probes.

ranking.statement: When an end-user application is assigned to several collections its probes are ranked by collection, 1 being the highest priority: Unified Communication, then Predefined Apps, then Custom Apps, in alphabetical order if the application is in several Custom Apps collections. Customized collections can be dragged and dropped to change their ranking; default collections cannot.

quotes: When you configure an application for the end user and the application is assigned to different collections, then the probes are ranked based on their collections as follows with 1 being the highest priority:
Unified Communication (Highest ranking)
2. Predefined Apps Collection
Custom Apps (Lowest ranking)
Alphabetical order if the application is in multiple Custom Apps collections.
You can drag and drop customized collections to alternate their ranking. Default collections cannot alternate their rankings (e.g., Unified Communication Collection).

collection-criteria.statement: Each end-user collection can configure Inclusion and Exclusion criteria based on the probing criteria; under End User Collection Settings the Exclusion Criteria and Probing Criteria cover fields that include User Groups, Location Groups, Zscaler Locations and Departments.

quotes: Each collection can configure Inclusion and Exclusion criteria based on the probing criteria.
Under Exclusion Criteria and Probing Criteria, you can configure policies for the following criteria:
User Groups
Location Groups
Zscaler Locations
Departments

collection-fields.statement: An end-user collection's settings include optional tags and an optional description.

quotes: Tags: (Optional) Select or create tags for the collection to easily identify your collection.
Description: (Optional) Enter a description of the collection.

remove-app.statement: An application cannot be removed from the Unified Communication Collection, nor from the Predefined Apps Collection if its status is Pending Onboard; removing an application from a collection removes it only for that collection.

quotes: You cannot remove an application from the Unified Communication Collection. You cannot remove an application from Predefined Apps Collection if its status is Pending Onboard.
If you remove the application from a collection, then it is only removed for that collection.

delete-app.statement: For End User Monitoring an application can be deleted from a custom collection or the Custom Apps Collection but not from the Unified Communication Collection or the Predefined Apps Collection, and its probes must be deleted before it; on the Managed Monitoring page the probe must be deleted before the application.

quotes: For End User Monitoring, you can delete an application from a custom collection or the Custom Apps Collection. You cannot delete an application from the Unified Communication Collection or the Predefined Apps Collection.
Prior to deleting an application, you must delete its corresponding probes.
For the Managed Monitoring page, you must delete the probe before you can delete an application.

delete-collection.statement: Per Managing Collections, deleting a collection also removes any applications and their associated probes under it, except that deleting an End User collection removes an application that is in several collections only from the deleted one; for Managed Monitoring the probes attached to an application must be deleted before a collection can be deleted.

quotes: Deleting a collection means you are also removing any applications and their associated probes under the collection. If you delete an End User collection where the application is in multiple collections, the application is only removed from that deleted collection.
For Managed Monitoring, you must delete the probes attached to an application before you can delete a collection.

enable-disable.statement: Disabling a collection disables the applications within it, and for an End User application that is in another collection only for the disabled collection; disabling an application disables all its probes, and for End User collections disables it for all collections; after any change in status the changes must be activated.

quotes: If you disable a collection, then you disable any applications within it. For End User collections, if the application is in another collection, then the application is only disabled for the disabled collection.

If you disable an application, then you disable all the probes associated with it. For End User collections, if the application is in another collection, then the application is disabled for all collections.
After any change in the status, you must activate the changes.

probe-counts.statement: The End User and Managed views have similar collection configurations and probe metrics, and some views might not show depending on the ZDX role and subscription level; for End User Monitoring the Configuration page gives the total number of enabled and disabled probes (Total) and the limited number of probes that can be configured (Limits).

quotes: Depending on your ZDX role and subscription level, you might not see some of the views.
The End User and Managed views have similar collection configurations and probe metrics.
Total: The total number of probes that are enabled and disabled.
Limits: The limited number of probes that can be configured.

limits.statement: The number of applications and probes that can be configured depends on the subscription level, and the subscription table's Collections row gives 1,000 in each of its four columns.

quotes: The number of applications and probes you can configure depends on your subscription level.

managed-default-collection-name.summary: The managed side's default collection is named differently: About Configuration calls it the Default Managed Collection, and Understanding Collections the Default Hosted Collection.

quotes: The Managed collection starts with the Default Managed Collection.

positions.says: The Managed collection starts with the Default Managed Collection.

quotes: Default Hosted Collection

positions.says: Understanding Collections names a Default Hosted Collection, alongside its statement that a configured application in the Hosted collection can only be in one collection.

managed-default-collection-name.impact: A search or an answer that uses one name misses the other; the pages do not say Hosted and Managed Monitoring are the same thing, though the Hosted collection's one-collection rule matches the Managed one.

managed-collection-delete.summary: Deleting a managed collection: Managing Collections requires the probes attached to an application to be deleted first, while Managing Zscaler Managed Probes says deleting a collection deletes all its probes and companion probes.

quotes: For Managed Monitoring, you must delete the probes attached to an application before you can delete a collection.

positions.says: For Managed Monitoring the probes attached to an application must be deleted before the collection.

quotes: If you delete a collection, then all probes and associated companion probes are deleted.

positions.says: Deleting a collection deletes all its probes and their companion probes.

managed-collection-delete.impact: Whether a managed collection with probes can be deleted directly, or only once its probes are gone, depends on which page is right; the pages do not say.

probe-deletion.summary: Whether a probe can be deleted on its own: Managing Collections says probes cannot be deleted by themselves, while Configuring a Probe gives a delete-probe procedure and Managing Zscaler Managed Probes says a probe and its companion can be deleted.

quotes: To remove probes, you must either delete the collection or delete the application. You cannot delete probes by themselves.

positions.says: Probes are removed only by deleting the collection or the application; they cannot be deleted by themselves.

quotes: To delete a probe for an application:

positions.says: Configuring a Probe gives a procedure for deleting a probe for an application.

quotes: You can delete a probe and its companion probe if they are no longer of use to you.

positions.says: A managed probe and its companion probe can be deleted.

probe-deletion.impact: The same Managing Collections article also requires an application's probes to be deleted before the application, so its own limitation and its deletion order disagree; whether a probe can be deleted alone is not settled.

collection-ranking.title: What ranking changes for an application in several collections, and how drag and drop combines with the alphabetical rule
collection-ranking.detail: The help ranks an end-user application's probes by collection and lets customized collections be dragged to change ranking. It does not say whose criteria apply or which probes run when an application is in several collections, nor how a dragged order combines with the alphabetical rule for several Custom Apps collections.
collection-ranking.blocks: explaining which probe or criteria wins for an application in several collections

managed-collection-criteria.title: Whether managed collections have criteria
managed-collection-criteria.detail: The captured articles list inclusion and exclusion criteria for End User collection settings. The Add Managed Collection form was read as listing a name, status, tags and description with no criteria step, but that is an absence found by comparison and no article states it.
managed-collection-criteria.blocks: answers about whom a managed collection's probes apply to

collections-api.title: How the contract's collection operations relate to the console's collections
collections-api.detail: The API contract has /v1/config/collections operations (list, create, read, update, delete, add application, import applications, rank and status); they were not read for this subject, so how they map to the console's default collections, ranking and deletion rules is not stated here.
collections-api.blocks: answers about managing collections through the API
